response.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount >= 2400 GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Every transaction row counts regardless of trans.type (credit PRIJEM, withdrawal VYDAJ, or the undocumented VYBER), because the request filters only on amount.
trans.amount is stored unsigned, so amount >= 2400 tests transaction size and not direction, as the verified notes state.
The request's 'trans.account_id' is the trans table's account_id column, and the average is the plain mean of the stored amounts with no rounding.
Accounts with tied transaction counts at the 10th position are cut off arbitrarily, since the request specifies no tiebreaker.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only credit transactions (type 'PRIJEM', money received) with amount at least 2400, using the documented +/- meaning of trans.type.
alternatives.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount >= 2400 AND type = 'PRIJEM' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;

alternatives.interpretation: Count only withdrawal transactions (type 'VYDAJ', money sent out) with amount at least 2400, using the documented +/- meaning of trans.type.
alternatives.sql: SELECT account_id, AVG(amount) AS avg_amount, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM trans WHERE amount >= 2400 AND type = 'VYDAJ' GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;
